These are small reproducible geometry fixtures, not musical works.

- `ruled-hooked-rests.json`: pixels from the original CC0 ReportLab exercises produced by `scripts/create-tab-32-corpus.py`. Includes missing pixel rows where TAB lines cross the symbol.
- `bravura-rests.json`: rest glyph pixels rendered by the installed VexFlow 4.2.5 Bravura glyph table, using `scripts/inspect-tab-rest-glyphs.mjs`. VexFlow is MIT licensed; the Bravura font is SIL OFL 1.1. The corresponding notices are included as `VexFlow-LICENSE.txt` and `Bravura-OFL.txt` (font source: https://github.com/steinbergmedia/bravura). This file tests independent standard glyph geometry, not score OCR answers.
- `joined-digits.json`, `exported-rests.json`, `curved-flag.txt`: small geometry crops from the original four-bar exercise generated by `scripts/verify-32-render.mjs`, printed by the app. Includes TAB-rule bridges, a partially masked rest and three curved flags. No user score content.

Full PDF inputs, oracle JSON, and per-case failure diagnostics are reproducible under `artifacts/32nd-support/fixtures` with the generator and benchmark scripts. No copyrighted user song is included here.

## Reproducing the benchmark

For the combined, self-contained model/OCR/photo check, see [Score quality laboratory](QUALITY-LAB.md). `npm run verify:score-quality` starts its own server, preserves the fixed regression floor, and generates a fresh seeded photo challenge.

Requires Node, Playwright with Chrome, Python with ReportLab and Pillow, and `pdftoppm` on PATH. Start the application on port 5174 (`npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5174`). Set `PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` to the Playwright ESM entry point available on the machine. The oracle stays in Node; only randomized-name PDF bytes enter the importer.

```powershell
python scripts/create-tab-32-corpus.py
node scripts/verify-tab-32-corpus.mjs candidate
node scripts/report-tab-32-corpus.mjs before candidate
node scripts/check-tab-32-regression.mjs tests/fixtures/thirty-second/baseline.json artifacts/32nd-support/candidate/report.json
node --test tests/thirty-second-support.test.mjs
npm test
npm run build
```

After generating the fixtures, `npm run verify:tab-32` runs recognition and the per-case regression gate together. It exits with an error if an import fails or a measured result falls below the checked-in floor.

The independent generator creates 36 PDFs (360 bars, 144 pages): three fonts and 12 conditions including 75/120/200 DPI, blur, JPEG damage, down/up scaling, thick/thin strokes, reversed stems, close beams, and an unused random seed. Each PDF has quarter/eighth/sixteenth/thirty-second patterns, mixed durations, triplets, sextuplets, rests, a tie, and frets 0–24. The held-out seed is fixed for repeatable regression; use a new seed via `--seed` for a genuinely new audit.

Every result retains the raw analysis, score document, compilation issues, elapsed time and page/bar/event failure diagnostics. `baseline.json` is a measured regression floor, **not** a claim of perfect recognition. The comparison fails on a drop in any case or duration, even if overall accuracy improves. Ties are measured separately; `documentStats.exactBars` tests notes/onsets/rhythm and does not include ties.

For app rendering, save/load, audio, and the app's own exported PDF:

```powershell
node scripts/verify-32-render.mjs
node scripts/verify-32-workspace.mjs
node scripts/verify-32-export-import.mjs
```

To repeat rendering in WebKit, set `WEBKIT_ONLY=1` and configure `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` for the installed browser engines, then run `verify-32-render.mjs`. This is desktop WebKit validation; an actual iPhone is a separate check.

When the user's private Flower Dance analysis is available, run `node scripts/check-tab-flower-regression.mjs baseline-analysis.json candidate-analysis.json`. This rejects extra rhythm positions as well as lost notes, chord names and techniques. The source PDF is deliberately not bundled.
